claims.text: An active-learning moment tensor potential can reproduce solid–liquid free-energy differences and fusion properties for elemental and binary metals.
The proposed framework can retain vibrational entropy, anharmonicity, and electron–vibration coupling in its fusion-property predictions.
The proposed framework will cost one to two orders of magnitude less than explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics workflows.
The proposed framework will be significantly faster than TOR-TILD.
Long ab initio molecular-dynamics trajectories can be replaced by a smaller set of ab initio training configurations for an active-learning MTP.
Densely sampling configurations within approximately 0.9–1.1 Tm will capture rare anharmonic and electron–vibration interactions accurately.
The intended operating window is approximately 0.9–1.1 times the melting temperature, with both solid and liquid phases represented.
Periodic boundary conditions and representative snapshots of both phases provide consistency in free-energy evaluation.
Local atomic configurations and short-range order inherently encode vibrational modes and anharmonic effects.
Local atomic configurations and short-range order inherently encode electron–vibration coupling features.
Active learning adds ab initio training points where model uncertainty is high, particularly near melting.
Thermodynamic integration using the refined MTP will yield phase free energies comparable in accuracy to full ab initio molecular-dynamics simulations.
Using the refined MTP for thermodynamic integration will greatly reduce computational cost.
Explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics and TOR-TILD workflows require extensive molecular-dynamics sampling to capture vibrational and anharmonic contributions.
The proposed method is tailored to elemental and binary systems near fusion.
Applicability of the proposed method to compositionally complex multicomponent alloys has not been established.
Prior studies on elemental and binary systems support using machine-learning potentials for free-energy evaluation.
Electron–vibration coupling may be captured inadequately if rare configurations are undersampled.
The method is falsified if its fusion free energies, melting temperature, or latent heat differ by more than 5% from explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics or TOR-TILD reference results.
